# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2026_bosutinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2026_bosutinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01672-y> (open access; the
  NONMEM control stream of the final model is Supplementary Table 4)

# Population

The model was fitted to 235 plasma bosutinib concentrations from 26 children
and adolescents with resistant or intolerant chronic-phase Philadelphia
chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia in the phase I dose-finding
part of the ITCC-054/COG AAML1921 trial (NCT04258943). Patients received oral
bosutinib once daily at 300 mg/m^2 (max 500 mg; n = 6), 350 mg/m^2 (max 600 mg;
n = 11) or 400 mg/m^2 (max 600 mg; n = 9) in 28-day cycles. Median age was 11.5
years (range 1-17; 1 infant, 12 children, 13 adolescents), median weight 44.8 kg
(12.0-115), median body surface area 1.32 m^2 (0.530-2.38); 15 were male and 11
female (Table 3 of the paper).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Wu_2026_bosutinib")()$population)
```

The structure is the adult bosutinib model of Garrett 2023 (two compartments,
first-order absorption with a lag time), with the adult covariates removed
(Asian race, creatinine clearance, age) and fixed-exponent allometric weight
scaling added. Adult priors were used through the NONMEM `$PRIOR NWPRI`
subroutine: informative on Q, V3 and ka, uninformative on the rest. Because the
pediatric data are oral only, bioavailability was fixed to the adult estimate
of 33.1%, so CL, V2, Q and V3 are systemic (not apparent) parameters.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg) | 74.9 L/h | Table 4 |
| `lvc` (V2 at 70 kg) | 1110 L | Table 4 |
| `lq` (Q at 70 kg) | 37.4 L/h | Table 4 |
| `lvp` (V3 at 70 kg) | 1960 L | Table 4 |
| `lka` | 0.366 1/h | Table 4 |
| `ltlag` | 0.467 h | Table 4 |
| `lfdepot` | 0.331 (fixed) | Table 4; Supplementary Table 4 `THETA(9) 0.331 FIX` |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods; Supplementary Table 4 `(BWT/70)**0.75` |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Methods; Supplementary Table 4 `(BWT/70)**1` |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, covariance | 0.312^2, 0.269^2, 0.0696 | Table 4 (IIV 31.2% and 26.9% CV; covariance 0.0696) |
| `etalq`, `etalvp`, covariance | 0.4, 0.4, 0.1 (fixed) | Table 4 (63.2% FIX, covariance 0.1 FIX); Supplementary Table 4 `$OMEGA BLOCK(2) FIX` |
| `etalka` | 0.917^2 | Table 4 (IIV 91.7% CV) |
| `etaiov_cl_1..3` | 0.471^2 | Table 4 (IOV 47.1% CV); Supplementary Table 4 `$OMEGA BLOCK(1)` + two `SAME` |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.0961) = 0.31 | Table 4 (proportional error, untransformed variance 0.0961) |
| Occasion indicators `oc1`, `oc2`, `oc3` | OCC = 1, 2, >= 3 | Supplementary Table 4 `FLAG1..FLAG3` |
| `cl <- exp(lcl + etalcl + iov_cl) * (WT/70)^0.75` etc. | n/a | Supplementary Table 4 `$PK` (`MU_1`..`MU_5`) |
| Two-compartment ODEs with depot | n/a | Supplementary Table 4 `ADVAN4 TRANS4`; Figure 1 |
| `f(depot)`, `alag(depot)` | n/a | Supplementary Table 4 `F1`, `ALAG1` |
| `Cc <- central / vc * 1000` | n/a | Supplementary Table 4 `S2 = V2` (dose in ug, DV in ng/mL) |
| `Cc ~ prop(propSd)` | n/a | Supplementary Table 4 `$ERROR Y = F*(1+EPS(1))` |

Table 4 reports the between-subject and between-occasion variability as %CV
equal to 100 times the square root of the variance: the fixed Q and V3
variances of 0.4 in the control stream are printed as 63.2% (= 100 * sqrt(0.4)).
The variances above are therefore (CV / 100)^2. The `$OMEGA` values printed in
the control stream (0.0966, 0.0706, 0.0706, 0.864, 0.2215) are the run's
initial estimates and agree with these to within 2-5%.

# Typical-value checks

The paper reports, for the 70-kg typical individual, an initial half-life of
6.38 h and a terminal half-life of 58.2 h (Results). These follow in closed form
from CL, V2, Q and V3, so they check the transcription of the four disposition
parameters.

```{r half-lives}
mod <- readModelDb("Wu_2026_bosutinib")
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
cl <- exp(p[["lcl"]])
vc <- exp(p[["lvc"]])
q <- exp(p[["lq"]])
vp <- exp(p[["lvp"]])
k10 <- cl / vc
k12 <- q / vc
k21 <- q / vp
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
r <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k21 * k10)
half_lives <- data.frame(
  phase = c("initial (alpha)", "terminal (beta)"),
  model_h = log(2) / c((s + r) / 2, (s - r) / 2),
  paper_h = c(6.38, 58.2)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model_h - paper_h) / paper_h)
knitr::kable(half_lives, digits = 2)
# The paper's half-lives were computed from its unrounded estimates; the
# 3-significant-figure parameters in Table 4 reproduce them to rounding.
stopifnot(all(abs(half_lives$pct_diff) < 1.5))
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated 5000 newly diagnosed (ND) and 5000 resistant/intolerant
(R/I) children aged 1 to < 18 years with age, weight and height drawn from the
NHANES August 2021-August 2023 survey, each dosed by the BSA bands of Table 2
for 28 days. NHANES microdata are not redistributed here; the cohort below uses
approximate sex-averaged CDC median weight- and height-for-age with lognormal
spread (weight CV about 20%, height CV about 4%), and is capped at 200 subjects
per arm. Body surface area is from the Mosteller formula, and the BSA is rounded
to the nearest 0.1 m^2 to pick the Table 2 band (bands below 0.3 m^2 use the
0.3 m^2 dose; 1.7 m^2 and above use the top band).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261117)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261117)

# Approximate CDC 2000 sex-averaged medians (maintainers' approximation).
growth <- data.frame(
  age = 1:18,
  wt = c(10, 12.5, 14.3, 16.3, 18.4, 20.7, 23, 25.6, 28.6, 32, 36, 40.5, 45.5, 50.5, 55, 59, 62, 64),
  ht = c(75, 87, 95, 102, 109, 115, 122, 128, 133, 138, 144, 150, 157, 163, 167, 170, 172, 173)
)

# Table 2: daily BSA-banded recommended phase II doses (mg).
bands <- data.frame(
  bsa_band = seq(0.3, 1.7, by = 0.1),
  dose_nd = c(100, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250, 275, 300, 325, 350, 400, 425, 450, 475, 500),
  dose_ri = c(125, 150, 200, 250, 275, 325, 350, 400, 450, 475, 525, 550, 600, 600, 600)
)

draw_children <- function(n, age_min, age_max) {
  age <- runif(n, age_min, age_max)
  wt <- approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = age, rule = 2)$y * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.2))
  ht <- approx(growth$age, growth$ht, xout = age, rule = 2)$y * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.04))
  bsa <- sqrt(wt * ht / 3600)
  # Integer band index (1 = 0.3 m^2 ... 15 = 1.7 m^2) avoids matching on
  # floating-point BSA values.
  idx <- pmin(pmax(round(bsa * 10) - 2L, 1L), nrow(bands))
  data.frame(AGE = age, WT = wt, BSA = bsa, bsa_band = bands$bsa_band[idx],
             dose_nd = bands$dose_nd[idx], dose_ri = bands$dose_ri[idx])
}

n_arm <- 200
arms <- bind_rows(
  draw_children(n_arm, 1, 18) |> mutate(arm = "ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", dose = dose_nd),
  draw_children(n_arm, 1, 18) |> mutate(arm = "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)", dose = dose_ri),
  draw_children(n_arm, 15, 18) |> mutate(arm = "ND, adult 400 mg (15-17 y)", dose = 400),
  draw_children(n_arm, 15, 18) |> mutate(arm = "R/I, adult 500 mg (15-17 y)", dose = 500),
  draw_children(n_arm, 15, 18) |> mutate(arm = "ND, RP2D (15-17 y)", dose = dose_nd),
  draw_children(n_arm, 15, 18) |> mutate(arm = "R/I, RP2D (15-17 y)", dose = dose_ri)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), OCC = 1L)
stopifnot(!anyNA(arms$dose))

# Once-daily dosing for 28 days; dense sampling over the day-14 and day-28
# dosing intervals (hours 312-336 and 648-672).
obs_times <- c(seq(312, 336, by = 0.5), seq(648, 672, by = 0.5))
dose_rows <- arms |>
  transmute(id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, ii = 24, addl = 27L, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- arms |>
  select(id) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, ii = 0, addl = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  left_join(arms |> select(id, WT, OCC, arm, AGE), by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(arms$id))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# PKNCA: steady-state exposure on days 14 and 28

Each dosing interval is re-anchored to start at 0 so PKNCA reads the trough at
the end of the 24-h interval.

```{r pknca}
nca_exposure <- function(sim) {
  nca_in <- sim |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    mutate(day = ifelse(time <= 336, "Day 14", "Day 28"),
           tad = ifelse(day == "Day 14", time - 312, time - 648)) |>
    select(id, arm, day, tad, Cc)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ tad | arm + day + id)
  dose_df <- nca_in |> distinct(id, arm, day) |>
    left_join(arms |> select(id, dose), by = "id") |>
    mutate(tad = 0)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ tad | arm + day + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                          tmax = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_wide <- function(nca) {
  out <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "ctrough", "cmax", "tmax")) |>
    select(id, arm, day, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
    left_join(arms |> select(id, AGE), by = "id")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(out$auclast), !anyNA(out$ctrough))
  out
}

nca <- nca_exposure(sim)
exposure <- nca_wide(nca)
```

## Comparison with Table 5 (BSA-banded RP2D, 1-17 years)

AUC is in 10^3 h*ng/mL and the trough in ng/mL, both as median [IQR].

```{r table-5}
fmt <- function(x, digits) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  sprintf("%s [%s-%s]", signif(q[2], digits), signif(q[1], digits), signif(q[3], digits))
}
table5_paper <- data.frame(
  arm = rep(c("ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)"), each = 2),
  day = rep(c("Day 14", "Day 28"), 2),
  auc_paper = c(2.42, 2.41, 3.17, 3.17),
  auc_iqr_paper = c("1.72-3.29", "1.71-3.28", "2.22-4.34", "2.22-4.38"),
  ctrough_paper = c(56.4, 55.9, 72.8, 74.9),
  ctrough_iqr_paper = c("32.9-87.6", "32.7-87.5", "43.7-114", "43.3-116")
)
table5_sim <- exposure |>
  filter(arm %in% table5_paper$arm) |>
  group_by(arm, day) |>
  summarise(
    auc_sim = median(auclast) / 1000,
    auc_sim_txt = fmt(auclast / 1000, 3),
    ctrough_sim = median(ctrough),
    ctrough_sim_txt = fmt(ctrough, 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
table5 <- left_join(table5_paper, table5_sim, by = c("arm", "day")) |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_paper) / auc_paper,
    ctrough_pct = 100 * (ctrough_sim - ctrough_paper) / ctrough_paper
  )
table5 |>
  transmute(
    Arm = arm, Day = day,
    `AUCtau paper` = paste0(auc_paper, " [", auc_iqr_paper, "]"),
    `AUCtau simulated` = auc_sim_txt,
    `AUC % diff` = round(auc_pct, 1),
    `Ctrough paper` = paste0(ctrough_paper, " [", ctrough_iqr_paper, "]"),
    `Ctrough simulated` = ctrough_sim_txt,
    `Ctrough % diff` = round(ctrough_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Centre of the distribution only: the cohort demographics approximate NHANES
# and the tails depend on which subjects are drawn. A mis-transcribed CL, F or
# dose unit moves every median by tens of percent; the pooled centre catches
# that, and the per-arm bound leaves room for the Monte Carlo error of a
# 200-subject median (about 5%).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(table5$auc_pct)) < 15,
  abs(median(table5$ctrough_pct)) < 15,
  all(abs(table5$auc_pct) < 30),
  all(abs(table5$ctrough_pct) < 30)
)
```

The same comparison through `ncaComparisonTable()` (day 28, AUC in h*ng/mL):

```{r nca-comparison}
reference <- data.frame(
  arm = c("ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)"),
  auclast = c(2410, 3170),
  ctrough = c(55.9, 74.9)
)
sim_long <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(day == "Day 28", arm %in% reference$arm,
         PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "ctrough")) |>
  select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_long, reference, by = "arm",
  units = c(auclast = "h*ng/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

## Comparison with Table 6 (adolescents 15-17 years)

```{r table-6}
table6_paper <- data.frame(
  arm = c("ND, adult 400 mg (15-17 y)", "R/I, adult 500 mg (15-17 y)",
          "ND, RP2D (15-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (15-17 y)"),
  auc_paper = c(1.74, 2.20, 2.14, 2.63),
  ctrough_paper = c(44.7, 55.3, 54.6, 66.2)
)
table6 <- exposure |>
  filter(day == "Day 28", arm %in% table6_paper$arm) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(auc_sim = median(auclast) / 1000, ctrough_sim = median(ctrough),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(table6_paper, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_paper) / auc_paper,
    ctrough_pct = 100 * (ctrough_sim - ctrough_paper) / ctrough_paper
  )
table6 |>
  transmute(
    Arm = arm,
    `AUCtau paper (10^3 h*ng/mL)` = auc_paper,
    `AUCtau simulated` = signif(auc_sim, 3),
    `AUC % diff` = round(auc_pct, 1),
    `Ctrough paper (ng/mL)` = ctrough_paper,
    `Ctrough simulated` = signif(ctrough_sim, 3),
    `Ctrough % diff` = round(ctrough_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  abs(median(table6$auc_pct)) < 15,
  abs(median(table6$ctrough_pct)) < 15,
  all(abs(table6$auc_pct) < 30),
  all(abs(table6$ctrough_pct) < 30)
)
# The paper's adult-dose / RP2D contrast within each indication: the RP2D
# raises adolescent exposure by 23% (ND) and 20% (R/I).
ratio <- with(table6, c(
  ND = auc_sim[arm == "ND, RP2D (15-17 y)"] / auc_sim[arm == "ND, adult 400 mg (15-17 y)"],
  RI = auc_sim[arm == "R/I, RP2D (15-17 y)"] / auc_sim[arm == "R/I, adult 500 mg (15-17 y)"]
))
ratio
stopifnot(all(ratio > 1))
```

## Inter-occasion variability in the simulation

The paper does not say whether its simulations drew the inter-occasion CL
variability. Re-solving the two 1-17-year RP2D arms with `OCC = 0` (no IOV term)
shows its effect on the spread: the log-scale interquartile width of the day-28
AUC is compared with the paper's (ln(3.28/1.71) = 0.65 for ND and
ln(4.38/2.22) = 0.68 for R/I).

```{r iov}
ids_main <- arms$id[arms$arm %in% c("ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)")]
sim_noiov <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events |> filter(id %in% ids_main) |> mutate(OCC = 0L),
  keep = c("arm", "AGE")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
exposure_noiov <- nca_wide(nca_exposure(sim_noiov))
iqr_width <- function(x) log(quantile(x, 0.75) / quantile(x, 0.25))
bind_rows(
  exposure |> filter(id %in% ids_main) |> mutate(iov = "IOV drawn (OCC = 1)"),
  exposure_noiov |> mutate(iov = "No IOV (OCC = 0)")
) |>
  filter(day == "Day 28") |>
  group_by(arm, iov) |>
  summarise(median_auc = signif(median(auclast) / 1000, 3),
            log_iqr_width = round(iqr_width(auclast), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper_log_iqr_width = ifelse(grepl("^ND", arm), 0.65, 0.68)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The paper's interquartile widths (also about 0.67 for the adolescent arms of
Table 6) fall between the two cases, nearer the IOV-drawn simulation. The IOV
term changes the spread, not the median.

## Age-group trend (Supplementary Table 5)

Supplementary Table 5 shows the day-28 AUC falling with age under the RP2D
(ND: 2.63, 2.52, 2.39, 2.18; R/I: 3.58, 3.48, 3.21, 2.66 x 10^3 h*ng/mL for ages
1-5, 5-9, 9-13 and 13-18 years), because BSA-based dosing scales with roughly
weight^0.67 while clearance scales with weight^0.75 relative to 70 kg.

```{r supp-table-5}
supp5 <- exposure |>
  filter(day == "Day 28", arm %in% c("ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)")) |>
  mutate(age_group = cut(AGE, c(1, 5, 9, 13, 18), include.lowest = TRUE,
                         labels = c("1-5", "5-9", "9-13", "13-18"))) |>
  group_by(arm, age_group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), auc_sim = signif(median(auclast) / 1000, 3),
            ctrough_sim = signif(median(ctrough), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(auc_paper = c(2.63, 2.52, 2.39, 2.18, 3.58, 3.48, 3.21, 2.66),
         ctrough_paper = c(56.6, 55.0, 57.8, 54.0, 76.2, 81.2, 80.4, 65.6))
knitr::kable(supp5)
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-5, fig.cap = "Simulated day-14 and day-28 AUCtau,ss and Ctrough under the BSA-banded RP2D, with the adult target ranges (+/-20%) shaded. Replicates Figure 5 of Wu 2026."}
targets <- data.frame(
  arm = c("ND, RP2D (1-17 y)", "R/I, RP2D (1-17 y)"),
  auc_lo = c(1.82, 2.52), auc_hi = c(2.72, 3.78),
  ct_lo = c(54.4, 72.8), ct_hi = c(81.6, 109)
)
fig5 <- exposure |>
  filter(arm %in% targets$arm) |>
  mutate(`AUCtau,ss (10^3 h*ng/mL)` = auclast / 1000, `Ctrough (ng/mL)` = ctrough) |>
  select(arm, day, `AUCtau,ss (10^3 h*ng/mL)`, `Ctrough (ng/mL)`) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(arm, day), names_to = "metric")
target_long <- bind_rows(
  targets |> transmute(arm, metric = "AUCtau,ss (10^3 h*ng/mL)", lo = auc_lo, hi = auc_hi),
  targets |> transmute(arm, metric = "Ctrough (ng/mL)", lo = ct_lo, hi = ct_hi)
)
ggplot(fig5, aes(day, value)) +
  geom_rect(data = target_long, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r figure-6, fig.cap = "Day-28 AUCtau,ss and Ctrough in adolescents (15-17 years) on the approved adult dose versus the BSA-banded RP2D. Replicates the pediatric arms of Figure 6 of Wu 2026 (the adult arms need the Garrett 2023 adult model, which is not in this package)."}
exposure |>
  filter(day == "Day 28", grepl("15-17", arm)) |>
  mutate(indication = ifelse(grepl("^ND", arm), "ND", "R/I"),
         regimen = ifelse(grepl("adult", arm), "Adult dose", "RP2D"),
         `AUCtau,ss (10^3 h*ng/mL)` = auclast / 1000, `Ctrough (ng/mL)` = ctrough) |>
  select(indication, regimen, `AUCtau,ss (10^3 h*ng/mL)`, `Ctrough (ng/mL)`) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(indication, regimen), names_to = "metric") |>
  ggplot(aes(regimen, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ indication, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r profiles, fig.cap = "Day-28 steady-state concentration-time profiles (median and 5th-95th percentiles) under the BSA-banded RP2D."}
sim |>
  filter(arm %in% targets$arm, time >= 648) |>
  group_by(arm, tad = time - 648) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose on day 28 (h)", y = "Bosutinib Cc (ng/mL)")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Virtual cohort.** The paper drew age, weight and height from NHANES
  2021-2023; that dataset is not redistributed here, so weight and height come
  from approximate CDC median growth curves with lognormal spread chosen by the
  maintainers. Ages are uniform over each age range. The exposures above are
  compared on medians only, which are less sensitive to these choices than the
  tails.
- **BSA bands.** Table 2 lists doses at BSA steps of 0.1 m^2 without stating
  how an intermediate BSA is assigned; BSA is rounded to the nearest 0.1 m^2
  here.
- **Inter-occasion variability.** Every simulated subject is given `OCC = 1`,
  so the occasion-1 IOV eta adds to the between-subject CL variability over the
  whole 28 days. The paper does not say how IOV was handled in its simulations.
  Pass `OCC = 0` to simulate without the IOV term.
- **A `non-mu referenced` warning is expected on model load.** The occasion
  indicators (`oc1 * etaiov_cl_1 + ...`) place the IOV etas outside a
  mu-referenced position, so rxode2 warns "some etas defaulted to non-mu
  referenced". This affects estimation efficiency, not simulation, and is
  shared by every IOV model in the library that uses occasion indicators.
- **Removed adult covariates.** The final control stream keeps the adult age
  effect on V2 and creatinine-clearance effect on CL with their exponents fixed
  to 0, and drops the Asian-race effects; these are listed under
  `covariatesDataExcluded` and have no effect in the model.
- **Zero-variance random effects.** The ETAs on the lag time and on F1 are
  `0 FIX` in the control stream and are omitted.
- **Adult comparator.** The adult arms of Table 6 and Figure 6 come from the
  Garrett 2023 adult model and are not reproduced.
- **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found in a literature search on
  2026-11-17.
